title: Instagram Is Bringing Amazon Affiliate Links Directly to Reels and Posts
gist: Meta's Instagram now lets US creators with 1,000+ followers attach up to 30 Amazon affiliate links per Reel and 20 per feed post, moving shopping links from bios into the feed ahead of the holidays, without taking a cut of sales; the move responds to social commerce competition from TikTok Shop.

insights.claim: Instagram now lets creators and businesses attach up to 30 Amazon affiliate links per video and 20 per regular feed post, limited to US-based adults with professional accounts over 1,000 followers.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: A new traffic and affiliate-commission channel for Amazon from Meta's feed, launched right before the holiday season.
insights.locator: Starting today, creators and businesses can attach

insights.claim: Tapping an Amazon product tile on an Instagram Reel opens an in-app page with the price, then hands the user off to the Amazon app or website to complete the purchase.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Amazon keeps checkout and transaction data while Instagram supplies discovery, deepening a Meta–Amazon commerce partnership.
insights.locator: In an example shared by Meta

insights.claim: Instagram will not take a cut of Amazon affiliate sales generated through the new links, at least for now, unlike TikTok's shopping model.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Meta is prioritizing engagement and creator retention over direct commerce take-rate; watch for a future monetization switch.
insights.quote: Unlike TikTok, however, Instagram will not take a cut of the sales (at least for now).
insights.locator: This change comes as social media shopping habits

insights.claim: Moving shopping links from creator bios directly into posts could undercut link-in-bio bundlers like Linktree, which arose because Instagram long allowed only one bio link (expanded to five in 2023).
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Platform-native linking features are an existential risk for third-party creator-link tools.
insights.locator: For years, Instagram users could attach a single external link

insights.claim: An analytics firm estimated about $19 billion of products were sold globally through TikTok Shop around a year earlier, roughly the size of eBay, pressuring Meta to expand shopping on Instagram.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Social commerce is reaching marketplace scale; competition for creator-driven sales is intensifying among Meta, TikTok and Reddit.
insights.locator: This change comes as social media shopping habits

insights.claim: Reddit is also experimenting with shopping heading into the holiday season through Reddit Reviews, which uses generative AI to summarize user sentiment about products.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Generative AI product summaries are becoming a commerce lever for social platforms.
insights.locator: Reddit is also experimenting with how users shop

insights.claim: Instagram claims its recommendation systems will not surface a sudden influx of shopping content, but WIRED warns that putting affiliate links directly in feeds could annoy users already inundated with ads.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: User-experience backlash is the key risk to Meta's feed-commerce push; watch engagement metrics.
insights.quote: We don’t expect a sudden influx of shopping content from this launch,
insights.locator: This latest attempt moves links from creator bios
